Source publication date: 2026-10-01

Presenc AI is building commercial infrastructure for the agentic web: the layer agents consult to discover, trust, price, and transact with businesses. AI brand visibility ships today as the live discovery layer.
Commercial infrastructure for the agentic web.
Best Open-Weight Robotics VLA Models 2026
Open-weight vision-language-action model comparison for October 2026: pi0.5, GR00T N1.7, MolmoAct2, X-VLA, OpenVLA-OFT, SmolVLA. LIBERO scores, licences, and the VRAM each one needs.
The leading open-weight vision-language-action models in October 2026 are pi0.5 from Physical Intelligence, GR00T N1.7 from NVIDIA, and MolmoAct2 from the Allen Institute for AI. pi0.5 is the usual research baseline and runs on a GPU with 8 GB of memory. GR00T N1.7 targets humanoids, and NVIDIA states it is commercially licensable. MolmoAct2 ships its training data and code along with the weights. SmolVLA from Hugging Face is the pick for low-cost arms and consumer hardware. A vision-language-action model, or VLA, takes camera images and a text instruction and outputs robot motor commands. This page covers downloadable models. For shipments, funding and manufacturers, see the humanoid robot market tracker . Open-Weight VLA Model Comparison Model Developer Parameters License Released LIBERO success rate and who ran it Hardware to run pi0.5 Physical Intelligence 3.6B Apache 2.0 (openpi repository) September 2025 96.85 average over four suites (Physical Intelligence) Over 8 GB of GPU memory for inference GR00T N1.7 NVIDIA 3B Apache 2.0 per GitHub, NVIDIA Open Model License per model card February 2026 97.65 Spatial, 98.45 Object, 97.5 Goal, 94.35 Long (NVIDIA) 16 GB or more of VRAM for inference MolmoAct2 Allen Institute for AI 5.4B Apache 2.0 for code. The model card carries no licence tag May 2026 97.2 average, 98.1 for the Think variant (AI2) Under 16 GB in bfloat16 for one fine-tuned checkpoint X-VLA X-VLA authors 0.9B Apache 2.0 November 2025 98.1 (X-VLA authors) Not stated OpenVLA-OFT OpenVLA-OFT authors 7.5B MIT February 2025 97.1 average over four suites (OpenVLA-OFT authors) About 16 GB of VRAM SmolVLA Hugging Face LeRobot 450M Apache 2.0 June 2025 87.3 average (Hugging Face paper) Consumer GPU or CPU OpenVLA OpenVLA project 7.5B MIT June 2024 76.5 average (as reported in the SmolVLA paper) Not stated All LIBERO figures are for checkpoints fine-tuned on LIBERO data. OpenVLA remains the most downloaded robotics model on Hugging Face, with about 289,000 downloads in the 30 days to October 1, 2026, ahead of GR00T N1.7 at about 147,000. VRAM Requirements Model Inference Fine-tuning Source pi0.5 Over 8 GB Over 22.5 GB with LoRA, over 70 GB for full fine-tuning openpi README GR00T N1.7 16 GB or more, including Jetson AGX Thor and Orin 40 GB or more recommended Isaac GR00T README MolmoAct2 Under 16 GB in bfloat16 for the bimanual YAM checkpoint. About 22 GB download per checkpoint Not stated MolmoAct2 repository OpenVLA-OFT About 16 GB for LIBERO, about 18 GB for ALOHA One to eight GPUs with 27 to 80 GB OpenVLA-OFT README SmolVLA Consumer GPU or CPU Single GPU SmolVLA paper Which to Pick for Which Job Humanoid or bimanual platform: GR00T N1.7. It is pretrained on humanoid data and 20,000 hours of human video, and exports to ONNX and TensorRT for Jetson. General arm manipulation baseline: pi0.5 through openpi or the LeRobot port. Full reproducibility: MolmoAct2. AI2 released weights, code and datasets, including 720 hours of bimanual data. Hobby and education arms such as SO-100: SmolVLA. The paper reports 78.3 percent average real-world success on three SO-100 tasks. Small model with a strong simulation score: X-VLA at 0.9B parameters. Licences: Open Weight Is Not Always Open Source Permissive. OpenVLA and OpenVLA-OFT are MIT. SmolVLA, X-VLA and the openpi repository are Apache 2.0. Check before shipping. NVIDIA's GitHub README says GR00T N1.7 is fully commercially licensable under Apache 2.0, while the Hugging Face card names the NVIDIA Open Model License and says the model is ready for commercial use. Its vision-language backbone, Cosmos-Reason2-2B, is a gated download. The earlier GR00T N1.6 card links to an NVIDIA non-commercial licence. The LeRobot ports of pi0 and pi0.5 are tagged with the Gemma licence on Hugging Face, which differs from the Apache 2.0 licence on the openpi repository. MolmoAct2 has an Apache 2.0 code repository, but its model card has no licence tag. Not open. The openpi README lists pi0, pi0-FAST and pi0.5 only. We found no open-weight release of later Physical Intelligence models. Caveats LIBERO is close to saturated. Five models report between 96 and just over 98 percent, so it no longer separates them. It is a simulation benchmark with one robot arm. Every score is self-reported. Each developer fine-tuned and tested its own model with its own settings. There is no neutral VLA leaderboard comparable to those for language models. Real robots score lower. AI2 reports 87.1 percent average for MolmoAct2 on real Franka arm tasks, with one multi-object task at 62 percent. A June 2026 third-party study on the SO-101 arm found performance "highly task-dependent" across pi0.5, SmolVLA and others. Base checkpoints are starting points. AI2 describes the MolmoAct2 base model as a foundation for fine-tuning, not a ready-to-run policy. Expect to collect demonstrations for your own robot. Brand Visibility Implications A VLA runs on a robot. Its output is movement, and nothing about it can be observed from outside the way a chat answer can. The visibility question is upstream. Robotics teams and hobbyists ask assistants which policy to start from, which arm to buy, and which simulator to use, and those answers shape what gets adopted. Model developers, robot makers and tooling vendors all have a stake in being described accurately there, including on licence terms that differ between a model card and a repository. Methodology This page is compiled from published sources, not from Presenc AI measurements. Parameter counts, licences and repository dates come from each model's Hugging Face card and the Hugging Face model API, read on October 1, 2026. Where a developer gives no release date, the month shown is the month the repository was created. Scores are quoted from the party that ran them and are labelled as such: developer model cards and papers, the GIFT-Eval leaderboard result files, the ViDoRe leaderboard as quoted on model cards, the openpi and Isaac GR00T repositories, and independent studies such as the Domyn guard model benchmark . Developer-reported scores use each developer's own test setup and are not directly comparable across rows. "Not reported" means we found no published score on that benchmark. Rankings in these categories change monthly. Status as of October 1, 2026. You describe your robot: its base, sensors, computer and what it should do. RoboStacker gives you: the ROS 2 packages it needs, in the order to bring them up the pieces still to add, like an odometry source for the EKF, a map for Nav2, or a sensor frame a workspace to download, with the robot model (URDF/xacro), ros2_control, EKF, Nav2 settings and launch files It covers warehouse robots, outdoor rovers (skid-steer and Ackermann), drones (PX4/ArduPilot companion computer) and robot arms (beta), on Humble and Jazzy. Every generated robot is built and tested automatically on each change, and the wheeled ones are driven through Nav2 on simulated motors. It’s free, and you don’t need an account to plan or download. I’d love to hear: Was anything unclear, or where did you get stuck? If you downloaded a workspace, did colcon build work for you? Did it miss anything for your robot? What would make it more valuable and useful for you? I’m exploring ideas like a Gazebo simulation of your exact robot, ready configs for common motor controllers, or a check-up script that compares your running robot to its plan. New ideas are very welcome! Thanks for taking a look. Happy to answer any questions here! The goal is to reduce reliance on dedicated welding fixtures by using one robot to grip and hold the workpiece while another welds it. video: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/986d984e-00fb-4769-97a7-4cb6e9866428 The grasping and welding components can also be used independently. The framework combines constraint-aware grasp sampling, weld seam extraction from CAD/mesh geometry, and motion planning with MoveIt 2. It targets ROS 2 Jazzy on Ubuntu 24.04. It’s currently a proof of concept demonstrated in simulation. Repository hold_and_weld_050 1920×1080 248 KB Constraint-aware grasp sampling The grasp sampler generates antipodal grasp candidates on exact CAD surfaces. Exclusion volumes keep grasps away from weld seams, screw holes and other forbidden regions. Candidates are filtered using gripper geometry and checked for collisions with the workpiece, secondary objects and the ground. STEP and URDF inputs are supported. hold_and_weld_141 1920×1080 220 KB Weld seam extraction The weld finder extracts seams from CAD and mesh geometry and exports weld paths as JSON. The mesh pipeline identifies contact boundaries between parts, traces them along the parts’ edges, and refines the resulting weld paths. hold_and_weld_272 1920×1080 201 KB Weld approach configuration and motion planning Reaching the start of a seam does not necessarily give the robot a suitable configuration for completing the weld. ConfigurationFinder selects the approach joint configuration before OMPL plans the approach. A custom Ceres-based IK solver minimizes position and orientation errors, with hard joint bounds and a seed penalty that favors configurations close to the seed. Multiple initial seeds explore alternative IK branches. Each candidate is evaluated along a sampled Cartesian path covering the plunge and weld motion. IK is solved at each sample using the previous solution as the seed. Candidates are rejected on IK failure, joint-limit violations, low Yoshikawa manipulability or excessive joint steps. Feasible candidates are ranked by their minimum joint-limit margin, minimum manipulability and distance from the home configuration. OMPL plans to the selected configuration as a joint goal. Pilz handles the plunge and linear/circular weld motions; other curves use a dense-waypoint Cartesian fallback. Dual-arm coordination Action servers handle grasping and welding, while a coordinator sequences the workcell: the gripper arm picks and holds the workpiece, then the welding arm executes the weld path. Separate launch files allow either side to run independently. Robot and gripper catalog Models and robot base poses are selected through workcell.yaml . Additional robot and gripper models can be easily integrated through xacro wrappers and catalog registration. A guide documents the required interfaces and configuration steps. Configurator and visualizers The workcell configurator lets you select robot and gripper models and position robots and scene objects using interactive markers in RViz2. Layouts are saved as YAML files, which can be copied into the workcell configuration. Separate visualizers display grasp candidates and weld paths. Testing and current limitations The repository includes unit tests. I also created a complex geometry example with concavities, elliptical surfaces and other geometric features to test grasp sampling and seam extraction. Results look good on the tested examples; additional geometry testing would help assess broader coverage. The complete workflow has been demonstrated in simulation. It has not yet been validated through physical welding trials. Existing physical demonstrations show that robot-held welding is feasible at smaller scales too. I’m actively working toward a hardware demonstration of this framework. The roadmap outlines planned development. Installation and documentation Prebuilt Docker image: docker pull ghcr.io/silanus23/hold_and_weld:0.3.0 The repository includes installation instructions, usage examples, package documentation and a guide for adding robot and gripper models. The problem: a default changes in a params file, the commit is called something like “update params”, and you find out when the robot behaves differently after an update. knoblog walks a repo’s git history, pulls out every parameter/gain/threshold/flag default from each commit, and writes down what changed, old → new, with the commit link. A real example from the Nav2 demo (nav2_bringup/params/nav2_params.yaml, commit 04c6ca5, Dec 13 2023): global_costmap.global_costmap.inflation_layer.inflation_radius 0.55 → 0.7 (+27.3%) local_costmap.local_costmap.inflation_layer.inflation_radius 0.55 → 0.70 (+27.3%) collision_monitor.FootprintApproach.time_before_collision 2.0 → 1.2 (−40%) In one commit, the default robot keeps further from obstacles and its collision monitor reacts with less lead time. Neither shows up in a changelog unless someone writes it down. Live demos (rebuilt weekly by a GitHub Action): Nav2 default parameters: Nav2 default-parameter changelog (demo) (the 100 most recent commits touching the params files) PX4 controller parameters: PX4 controller-parameter changelog (demo) What it reads today: ROS 2 ros__parameters YAML, including multi-node files like nav2_params.yaml. Arrays are diffed per element ( max_accel[0] 2.5 → 3.0 ), and 1 vs 1.0 is kept distinct because ROS 2 cares about int vs double. PX4 module.yaml / *_params.yaml and legacy PARAM_DEFINE_* . A move from .c to .yaml is shown as a move. ArduPilot AP_GROUPINFO tables and GSCALAR / ASCALAR defaults (the newest and least tested part). Plain YAML/JSON/TOML and C/C++/Python/Rust constants. Outputs are a static HTML site, an Atom feed, changes.json for your own tooling, and optional post text. It’s deterministic: values are quoted from the diff, never generated. An LLM summary is optional and off unless you configure it. Limits, so nobody is surprised: It only sees what’s committed in the repo. Your own overrides, launch-file arguments and values set at runtime aren’t covered. Needs Python 3.11+, so on Humble / Ubuntu 22.04 (system Python 3.10) use the GitHub Action or a newer interpreter. It’s v0.1.1 and has been tested on Nav2, PX4 and ArduPilot history, not much else yet. Try it: pip install knoblog knoblog init --preset ros2 # writes knoblog.yml; set watch.paths to your params files knoblog run --repo . --config knoblog.yml --out site or in CI with uses: fitzyracing1/knoblog@v0 . Source (MIT): GitHub - fitzyracing1/knoblog: Plain-English changelogs, Atom/JSON feeds and X-ready post text for parameter, gain, threshold, flag and config changes (ROS 2, PX4, ArduPilot, C/C++, YAML/JSON/TOML). GitHub Action + CLI. · GitHub Questions I’d really like answers to: Would a per-commit list like this be useful for your team, or do you track default changes some other way? Which parameter formats or repos should it handle next (MoveIt configs, ros2_control, Autoware)? Is “old → new + % change” the right level of detail, or would you want something else, like the related PR or the doc string? Thanks for reading. Bug reports and “this is wrong for X” are very welcome. The Monitor’s built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server connects an MCP-compatible AI assistant to the system information and operations available in the Monitor. You can ask questions about the running system and inspect the resulting entities, charts and operations in the workspace. The preview demonstrates four workflows: Explore discovered applications, topics, publishers and subscribers. Create graphs from selected topic fields. Investigate a communication problem using endpoint configuration, including a reliability QoS mismatch. Publish sample data to a selected topic in a test environment and observe the response. For ROS 2 deployments using DDS, the connection is the underlying DDS topics and endpoints. The Monitor works at that layer; this is not a claim that it understands every ROS graph concept or supports every ROS middleware implementation. Fast DDS Pro can also be integrated into ROS 2 and Vulcanexus to provide additional communication capabilities and professional tools. That integration is distinct from the requirements for inspecting a particular system with the Monitor. The linked videos demonstrate the DDS workflows. For a specific ROS 2 setup, compatibility and the available operations depend on the middleware, versions, topic type information and configuration. DDS Monitor Pro is a commercial product. These new capabilities are in final testing, with release expected in the coming weeks. The MCP server starts disabled. Once enabled, connected clients can invoke supported operations without a separate approval prompt for each action, so use trusted clients and a test environment for publishing data. HuggingFace 与 GitHub 公开。在覆盖 11 类感知能力的 34 项 grounding 基准、对比 44 个基线模型的评测中，GroundingPI 平均得分 73.68%，超过参数量更大的 GPT-6 Astra（71.54%）。 模型定位与技术方案 GroundingPI 面向物理智能（Physical Intelligence）场景的精确定位需求。论文称，现有视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型与世界-动作模型（WAM）的感知能力普遍来自通用视觉-语言模型或视频生成基座，在密集遮挡、微小目标和闭环控制所需的低延迟定位场景下仍不稳定。GroundingPI 以精确点（point）和边界框（box）作为视觉基元，将坐标量化后纳入与文本共享的词表，用同一套输出协议统一目标检测、指代表达理解、指向、OCR、GUI 元素定位和文档版面六类定位任务。 训练采用三阶段方案：多模态与空间预训练、监督微调（SFT）、基于 GRPO 的强化学习，数据来自公开数据集与团队自建的数据引擎。项目页披露的消融数据显示，预训练数据规模从第一阶段逐步扩展至第四阶段，grounding 平均分从 61.69% 升至 73.68%；在数据配比消融中，六组数据全量组合在下游迁移中表现最好，仅用物理智能数据的对照组成绩明显落后。 模型规格方面，HuggingFace 模型卡显示，GroundingPI 以 BF16 精度存储约 48.4 亿参数，权重约 9.8GB（两个分片），支持中英双语，基于 transformers 库的自定义 image-text-to-text 架构，并附在线 Demo Space。 面向物理智能的下游迁移 论文将 GroundingPI 作为下游视觉基座接入统一的动作专家（Action DiT）进行受控对比，固定动作专家架构、动作数据与训练预算（4 万步更新、40 张加速卡），仅更换预训练基座。对照模型覆盖四类基座：通用视觉语言模型（Qwen3-VL-4B、PaliGemma-3B）、视频生成基座（Wan2.2-TI2V-5B、Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B）、grounding 模型（LocateAnything-3B、Rex-Omni-3B）与具身基座模型（RynnBrain 系列）。 下游评测 指标 GroundingPI-4B 最强对照 (“FFR”) (NASDAQ: FFR) jointly held a series new product launch event. The companies announced that two new robots have officially joined the “One Brain, Multi-forms, Multi-capabilities” FF Robot World 2.0: FF Nova, an entry-level embodied AI humanoid robot priced below $2,500, and FF Nova Mini, a humanoid robot for foundational Physical AI education. The financing is priced at market, with no discount or no warrants, and low associated financing costs, and is structured to minimize equity dilution. Upon closing, on an as-converted, fully diluted basis, FFAI will hold approximately 65.7% of FFR, with all newly issued shares received in this transaction subject to an 18-month lockup. Management and employees will hold approximately 18.2%, PIPE investors approximately 5.5%, and other FFR stockholders approximately 10.7%. PIPE investors may not sell their shares within six months or before the resale registration statement becomes effective. FFAI, management and employees, and PIPE investors will collectively hold approximately 89.3%. Excluding these holdings, the freely tradable public float will consist of approximately 13 million shares, representing approximately 10.7% of the total. The signing of these agreements is expected to provide benefits in three key areas. From the capital perspective, the relatively limited public float is expected to reduce the near-term supply of freely tradable shares, supporting the goal of maximizing stockholder value. From the financial perspective, FFR is expected to have almost no debt after closing and move forward with a lighter structure. REKI: Registering Knowledge in VLAs
Submitted 15 Oct 2026 en REKI: Registering Knowledge in VLAs Kyutai INRIA École nationale des ponts et chaussées JM Juliette Marrie PP Paul Pacaud AR Adrien Ramanana Rahary SC Shizhe Chen MB Moritz Böhle Abstract We introduce REKI, a 2.4B vision-language-action model (VLA) pretrained exclusively on public data that sets a new Pareto frontier between performance and model size: on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin Clean2Rand and RoboCasa365, it is outperformed only by models about twice its size. REKI consists of a vision-language model (VLM) followed by a flow-matching action expert, and is pretrained on a curated mixture of public robot, egocentric human and vision-language data. Additionally, we endow it with a memory that gives the policy access to its recent past at negligible cost: a few register tokens in the action expert summarise the output of the VLM at each frame and persist in the expert's cache. This memory improves success in simulation and on real robots , [p 12 ] and makes oscillations between poses about four times rarer . [p 9 ] REKI uses a simple model design and training paradigm, and is optimised to be efficient at training and inference. We release the full code across data curation, training, inference and evaluation, deployment, and all pretrained and finetuned model weights: this https URL. View Paper PDF 5 Save Cite AI Overview Copy Edit Picture a UR5 arm told to place three fruits into plates. Halfway through, the scene can look much like it did a moment ago, and a single camera frame doesn't reveal which fruit has already been moved or what the arm just tried. REKI's answer is to give the policy a short recent past without paying to re-encode old images: learned register tokens in the action model summarize each frame, and their cached keys and values are reused when the next action chunk is generated. [p 1 ] An autonomous UR5 rollout of a fruit-placing task, a real-robot example of the kind of task where tracking progress matters. The clip itself is not a memory-on versus memory-off comparison. On the real robot, memory helps on longer-horizon tasks. Each task used ten test episodes, and scores include partial credit, so they are not full-success rates. A short history, stored in the action model REKI is a vision-language-action (VLA) model, meaning it maps an instruction and camera views to robot actions. A vision-language model (VLM) encodes the instruction and the views. A flow-matching action expert then predicts the next chunk of robot actions. REKI has 2.4B parameters and is pretrained on public robot data. [p 1 ] The memory lives in the action expert. Alongside the noisy action chunk, the expert carries 32 learned registers. A frame's registers attend to that frame's encoded context and to earlier registers. The current action tokens read both the current and the cached registers, while the registers never read the action tokens. Their keys and values persist in a rolling cache. [p 4 ] The usual window is three frames: the current one plus two earlier ones, sampled one second apart in training. Because cached registers can themselves absorb information from earlier ones, the rolling window is not a strict limit on how far information can persist. [p 4 ] At inference, each frame is encoded only once. Its registers are computed on the first of ten Euler denoising steps and reused on the later steps, and the oldest frame is dropped as the window rolls forward. [p 6 ] The paper reports that reading cached registers adds 0.1 ms and under 1% to prediction time in its measured setup. That is a timing measurement on one setup, not a claim that memory costs nothing in general. In training, a window of frames is batched rather than unrolled step by step, and each frame's action chunk gets its own loss. [p 5 ] The idea extends earlier work. Qwen-RobotManip also uses register-like tokens in its action expert, but, per REKI's account, discards them after each forward pass; REKI keeps their keys and values across frames. HAMLET summarizes frames with moment tokens and combines them in a separate memory module, whereas REKI puts registers inside the existing action expert's attention. The paper does not report a direct benchmark comparison against HAMLET or other history methods. Panel (a) shows instruction and camera views flowing through the VLM into the action expert, with past register keys and values entering through self-attention and a cache. Panel (b) zooms into one expert block: action tokens read current and past registers and each other, but registers do not read action tokens. What history changes, and what it does not The cleanest test holds the weights fixed and changes only how much history is available at evaluation. Labels below read as frames at finetuning → frames at evaluation. On LIBERO-Plus (40 LIBERO tasks under seven perturbation dimensions), a model finetuned and evaluated with three frames scores 90.4% success, versus 88.9% for the same weights evaluated without memory, essentially matching a separately trained memoryless model at 88.9%. The pattern is similar on RoboTwin Clean and RoboCasa365, so most of the gain comes from reading past frames at inference rather than from training on windows. There is one exception to "more memory is better": on RoboCasa365, evaluating the three-frame model with two frames scores 39.3%, slightly above the 38.4% with three. [p 9 ] The memory also changes a specific failure pattern. The authors define an oscillating episode as one where an arm moves in roughly opposite directions across at least three consecutive chunks, ignoring small movements. Fewer than 5% of such episodes succeed. On RoboTwin Clean, removing history at evaluation from the same weights raises the share of oscillating episodes from 4.1% to 14.8%; one past frame gives 4.6%, and a model trained and evaluated without memory sits at 18.6%. The effect is larger in two-arm tasks. The criterion was set using 16 of RoboTwin's 50 tasks and the effect confirmed on the other 34. [p 9 ] The authors attribute this to perceptual aliasing: two visually similar poses can trigger chunks that bounce between them, and short history can disambiguate how the robot arrived. That is their interpretation of an observed reduction, not a proven cause, and the result does not show that every oscillating episode is rescued. Success rates and oscillation rates across memory settings (finetuning → evaluation: 3 → 3, 3 → 2, 3 → 1, 1 → 1), a breakdown of oscillation by one-arm and two-arm tasks, and per-chunk time on one H100. Panels do not share an axis. The real-robot results point the same way. Removing memory leaves the two shorter-horizon tasks unchanged (65 vs. 65 and 57.5 vs. 57.5) but lowers scores on the three longer-horizon tasks by 12 to 17.5 percentage points. [p 11 ] A baseline others can test The evidence supports short recent context helping on these tasks, not that registers can carry information about events far in the past, which the paper says remains untested. [p 12 ] On openness, the authors present REKI as a fully released pipeline, but the repository README says the pretraining code and data pipeline will come in a later update. REKI: Registering Knowledge in VLAs
Submitted 15 Oct 2026 en REKI: Registering Knowledge in VLAs Kyutai INRIA École nationale des ponts et chaussées Juliette Marrie PP Paul Pacaud AR Adrien Ramanana Rahary SC Shizhe Chen MB Moritz Böhle Abstract We introduce REKI, a 2.4B vision-language-action model (VLA) pretrained exclusively on public data that sets a new Pareto frontier between performance and model size: on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin Clean2Rand and RoboCasa365, it is outperformed only by models about twice its size. REKI consists of a vision-language model (VLM) followed by a flow-matching action expert, and is pretrained on a curated mixture of public robot, egocentric human and vision-language data. Additionally, we endow it with a memory that gives the policy access to its recent past at negligible cost: a few register tokens in the action expert summarise the output of the VLM at each frame and persist in the expert's cache. This memory improves success in simulation and on real robots , [p 12 ] and makes oscillations between poses about four times rarer . [p 9 ] REKI uses a simple model design and training paradigm, and is optimised to be efficient at training and inference. We release the full code across data curation, training, inference and evaluation, deployment, and all pretrained and finetuned model weights: this https URL. View Paper PDF 12 Save Cite AI Overview Copy Edit Picture a UR5 arm told to place three fruits into plates. Halfway through, the scene can look much like it did a moment ago, and a single camera frame doesn't reveal which fruit has already been moved or what the arm just tried. REKI's answer is to give the policy a short recent past without paying to re-encode old images: learned register tokens in the action model summarize each frame, and their cached keys and values are reused when the next action chunk is generated. [p 1 ] An autonomous UR5 rollout of a fruit-placing task, a real-robot example of the kind of task where tracking progress matters. The clip itself is not a memory-on versus memory-off comparison. On the real robot, memory helps on longer-horizon tasks. Each task used ten test episodes, and scores include partial credit, so they are not full-success rates. A short history, stored in the action model REKI is a vision-language-action (VLA) model, meaning it maps an instruction and camera views to robot actions. A vision-language model (VLM) encodes the instruction and the views. A flow-matching action expert then predicts the next chunk of robot actions. REKI has 2.4B parameters and is pretrained on public robot data. [p 1 ] The memory lives in the action expert. Alongside the noisy action chunk, the expert carries 32 learned registers. A frame's registers attend to that frame's encoded context and to earlier registers. The current action tokens read both the current and the cached registers, while the registers never read the action tokens. Their keys and values persist in a rolling cache. [p 4 ] The usual window is three frames: the current one plus two earlier ones, sampled one second apart in training. Because cached registers can themselves absorb information from earlier ones, the rolling window is not a strict limit on how far information can persist. [p 4 ] At inference, each frame is encoded only once. Its registers are computed on the first of ten Euler denoising steps and reused on the later steps, and the oldest frame is dropped as the window rolls forward. [p 6 ] The paper reports that reading cached registers adds 0.1 ms and under 1% to prediction time in its measured setup. That is a timing measurement on one setup, not a claim that memory costs nothing in general. In training, a window of frames is batched rather than unrolled step by step, and each frame's action chunk gets its own loss. [p 5 ] The idea extends earlier work. Qwen-RobotManip also uses register-like tokens in its action expert, but, per REKI's account, discards them after each forward pass; REKI keeps their keys and values across frames. HAMLET summarizes frames with moment tokens and combines them in a separate memory module, whereas REKI puts registers inside the existing action expert's attention. The paper does not report a direct benchmark comparison against HAMLET or other history methods. Panel (a) shows instruction and camera views flowing through the VLM into the action expert, with past register keys and values entering through self-attention and a cache. Panel (b) zooms into one expert block: action tokens read current and past registers and each other, but registers do not read action tokens. What history changes, and what it does not The cleanest test holds the weights fixed and changes only how much history is available at evaluation. Labels below read as frames at finetuning → frames at evaluation. On LIBERO-Plus (40 LIBERO tasks under seven perturbation dimensions), a model finetuned and evaluated with three frames scores 90.4% success, versus 88.9% for the same weights evaluated without memory, essentially matching a separately trained memoryless model at 88.9%. The pattern is similar on RoboTwin Clean and RoboCasa365, so most of the gain comes from reading past frames at inference rather than from training on windows. There is one exception to "more memory is better": on RoboCasa365, evaluating the three-frame model with two frames scores 39.3%, slightly above the 38.4% with three. [p 9 ] The memory also changes a specific failure pattern. The authors define an oscillating episode as one where an arm moves in roughly opposite directions across at least three consecutive chunks, ignoring small movements. Fewer than 5% of such episodes succeed. On RoboTwin Clean, removing history at evaluation from the same weights raises the share of oscillating episodes from 4.1% to 14.8%; one past frame gives 4.6%, and a model trained and evaluated without memory sits at 18.6%. The effect is larger in two-arm tasks. The criterion was set using 16 of RoboTwin's 50 tasks and the effect confirmed on the other 34. [p 9 ] The authors attribute this to perceptual aliasing: two visually similar poses can trigger chunks that bounce between them, and short history can disambiguate how the robot arrived. That is their interpretation of an observed reduction, not a proven cause, and the result does not show that every oscillating episode is rescued. Success rates and oscillation rates across memory settings (finetuning → evaluation: 3 → 3, 3 → 2, 3 → 1, 1 → 1), a breakdown of oscillation by one-arm and two-arm tasks, and per-chunk time on one H100. Panels do not share an axis. The real-robot results point the same way. Removing memory leaves the two shorter-horizon tasks unchanged (65 vs. 65 and 57.5 vs. 57.5) but lowers scores on the three longer-horizon tasks by 12 to 17.5 percentage points. [p 11 ] A baseline others can test The evidence supports short recent context helping on these tasks, not that registers can carry information about events far in the past, which the paper says remains untested. [p 12 ] On openness, the authors present REKI as a fully released pipeline, but the repository README says the pretraining code and data pipeline will come in a later update. 联合研发的世界动作模型LoopWAM，登顶真机评测榜单RoboChallenge Table30 V2，成功率与过程分双双位列榜首，成绩超过VLA-DM0.5等同期方案。同时，LoopWAM在仿真榜单RoboTwin 2.0和RoboCasa365上同样取得SOTA表现。 LoopWAM在所有榜单评测中使用的模型，均由 国产卡阿里云 PPU-810E 训练， 非NVIDIA 系列卡。 这一成绩背后，是一条从真实部署中持续学习的技术路线：让成功、次优和失败经验共同拓展世界模型的学习范围，增强对任务过程和动作后果的理解，再通过质量引导提升动作生成，使机器人在下一轮部署时做得更好。 从仅使用专家演示训练的初始模型出发，经过三轮部署与训练，LoopWAM的整体成功率提高了约19.7个百分点，相对提升 约83% ，过程分也从36.10提升至 56.80 。 让真实部署经验成为下一轮进步的起点，是LoopWAM此次登顶的关键。 这种从真实部署反馈中持续迭代的思路，与Physical Intelligence近日发布的PI API workflow不谋而合：通过“数据上传—模型微调—机器人部署—评估与数据收集”的循环推进能力提升。LoopWAM则在部署数据的利用上更进一步：闭环更新无需额外采集专家演示，也无需引入强化学习，而是发挥世界模型从动作与环境变化中学习的特点，将成功、次优和失败的rollout轨迹全部纳入视频预测训练，再通过质量steering与加权动作监督提升动作生成质量，让部署经验本身成为持续自提升的来源。 图1 PI API（来源：Physical Intelligence） 01 30项真机任务检验综合能力 RoboChallenge Table30 V2覆盖ALOHA、DOS-W1、ARX5和UR5四种机器人本体，包含物品整理、工具使用、精细操作和双臂协同等多类任务。 图2 RoboChallenge 多任务可视化 真实操作中的挑战，存在于每一次接触与运动之中：能否选对目标，能否稳定抓取，能否把工具用到位，又能否连续完成多个操作步骤。Table30 V2通过成功率和过程分，分别衡量任务完成情况与执行过程的完成质量。 在本次评测中，LoopWAM在11项任务上的成功率达到 60% 及以上，9项任务过程分达到80分及以上。几组具体成绩，让模型能力更加直观： 整理水果、物品分类、取出绿色积木：成功率均为 100% 用小勺舀取物体：成功率 90% ，过程分 92 按下按钮：成功率 80% ，过程分 92.5 堆叠碗具：成功率 80% ，过程分 89 从辨认目标、完成分类，到操作工具、推进多阶段任务，高分表现分布在不同本体和任务类型上，共同支撑了LoopWAM的综合成绩。 02 让成功与失败经验进入学习闭环 登顶背后，LoopWAM关注的是一个直接影响机器人持续进步的问题：真实部署中积累的经验，怎样才能被用好？ 专家演示为机器人提供了优质的学习起点。但进入真实环境后，机器人会遇到演示之外的状态：抓取发生偏移、物体意外滑落、工具接触不充分，或者任务只完成了一部分。 这些部署轨迹包含了丰富的物理交互信息，也混杂着质量不同的动作。把所有动作都当作模仿目标，可能强化不理想的行为；只保留成功轨迹，又会丢掉大量关于动作及其后果的经验。 LoopWAM由此提出一种闭环世界动作模型：把成功、次优与失败经验纳入统一训练，用更广泛的真实交互增强世界建模，再通过质量引导和动作监督加权，让策略吸收经验的同时保持对高质量行为的偏向。 图3 LoopWAM闭环自提升 这项工作的完整名称是LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts。贯穿其中的流程可以概括为： 部署 → 收集成功、次优与失败轨迹 → 质量感知训练 → 再部署。 每一轮新经验都会与专家演示和此前积累的轨迹共同进入训练，形成持续迭代的闭环。 03 支撑闭环自提升的关键技术 LoopWAM围绕一个目标展开：充分利用真实部署中的各种经验，增强世界模型对任务与物理交互的理解，并将这种理解转化为更高质量的动作。为此，它把数据分布扩展、动作条件世界建模、视频与动作联合生成，以及质量感知学习结合起来。LoopWAM以Wan2.2-TI2V-5B预训练视频模型为基础，构建视频与动作双分支架构，联合预测同一时间范围内的未来画面与机器人动作。 图4 LoopWAM方法 吸收更多真实部署数据，拓展世界模型的学习范围 专家演示提供完成任务的优质路径，真实部署则带来更广泛的状态、动作及其结果。LoopWAM将成功、次优和失败轨迹都纳入训练，保留所有质量轨迹的视频预测监督。更丰富的交互过程由此成为世界模型的学习材料，拓展其对环境变化和物理交互的表征能力。 强化ACWM，让模型学清动作带来的后果 LoopWAM在同一世界动作模型中强化动作条件世界建模（Action-Conditioned World Modeling，ACWM）：利用已执行的动作，预测它们对应的视觉结果。其关键是来源相关的噪声采样，分别控制视频与动作在训练中的噪声水平。 对于专家演示，模型从较强噪声中恢复专家执行对应的未来画面，同时学习动作生成，让模型能够学到如何完成任务。对于部署轨迹，则对动作施加较小的噪声，保留更多动作信息，让视频分支据此学习动作会引起的环境变化。即使任务没有完成，动作与结果之间的联系仍能用于训练，促进预测视频与生成动作在行为及结果上的一致性。 让世界建模直接参与动作生成 在同一次联合去噪过程中，视频与动作信息通过每一层的双向注意力持续交互。丰富的视频预测监督帮助模型学到更好的物理世界表征和动作后果知识，二者共同支持动作生成：模型既学习“任务怎样最优完成”，也学习“生成的动作会怎样改变环境”，让世界模型更充分地支持机器人控制。 区分数据质量，引导生成高质量动作 为了让模型在吸收更多经验的同时清楚行为优劣，LoopWAM为轨迹赋予质量分数，并将质量条件加入任务指令，通过质量steering的方式驱动视频与动作分支。训练时，模型学习同一任务下不同质量的行为分布；真实部署时，指定专家质量条件，将生成引导到高质量行为分布。 质量条件之外，LoopWAM还根据轨迹质量调整动作监督的权重。在所有轨迹都保留完整视频预测监督的同时： 专家轨迹提供完整的动作监督。 次优轨迹按质量加权，降低对较差动作的模仿强度。 失败轨迹的直接动作监督权重设为零，其真实交互后果仍用于世界建模。 质量steering负责区分不同的行为分布，监督权重决定各类动作被模仿的程度。二者共同作用，让模型从更广泛的经验中学习世界，并引导动作生成偏向高质量行为，支持真实部署的闭环自提升。 图5 四项任务的视频预测 上面的动图展示了整理水果、收纳笔、堆叠碗具和滚筒除尘四项任务上的视频预测效果。每组左侧是机器人执行时的真实观测（Obs），右侧是模型预测（Pred）。对照可见，预测视频能够反映机械臂运动、物体移动和操作进程，直观呈现了视频和动作预测在主要运动和操作进程上的一致性。 这种一致性由训练与生成机制共同促进：训练时，丰富的交互数据提供动作与实际结果之间的对应关系，来源相关的噪声采样强化ACWM，使模型学习动作会引起的环境变化；生成时，视频与动作在同一次联合去噪中通过双向注意力持续交换信息，让对未来的预测与正在生成的动作相互关联。 04 三轮部署带来持续提升 闭环是否有效，可以直接看三轮部署的变化。在覆盖30项任务的Table30 V2实验中，LoopWAM持续吸收自身的真实部署经验，并通过三轮闭环更新提升多任务表现。 整体成功率：23.67% → 28.00% → 37.67% → 43.33%。 过程分：36.10 → 42.63 → 51.65 → 56.80。 图6 多任务自提升 三轮更新中，两项总体指标每轮均有提高。这组结果表明，LoopWAM能够将自身在多任务环境中积累的部署经验，转化为后续策略改进。 05 叠衣服任务中的持续自提升 面对困难单任务的后训练，LoopWAM同样能够利用真实部署经验持续提升。在叠衣服任务上，LoopWAM能够从随意丢到机器人面前、杂乱的衣物开始操作。衣物的初始状态混乱且复杂多样：褶皱与堆叠会遮住衣角，适合抓取的位置也随姿态变化而变化。 机器人需要先在混乱状态下寻找合适的抓取位置，通过反复抓取与逐步展开，让衣物边角暴露出来，再抓住衣角完成后续折叠。衣物会随着操作不断变形，这要求模型根据每一步的实际变化持续调整动作。 LoopWAM从多任务模型出发，先使用新采集的专家叠衣演示进行单任务后训练，再开展两轮部署驱动的自提升。 叠衬衫成功率由13.20%提升至32.54%，最终达到55.56%；过程分从14.44提升至67.78。 图7 叠衣服后训练自提升 图8 叠衣服效果展示（操作部分10倍速） 这说明，在模型已经针对一个困难任务完成适配后，继续利用真实执行反馈，仍然能够带来明显增益。 06 在仿真基准中进一步验证 在两个仿真基准上，LoopWAM进一步验证了更广泛意义下的自提升：模型更新可以利用任意已部署策略产生的轨迹，即使这些策略的表现较差。来自不同策略的部署经验扩展了可学习的状态、动作与结果分布，LoopWAM通过质量感知训练从中学习世界变化，并引导动作生成偏向高质量行为。 在包含50项双臂任务的RoboTwin 2.0上，LoopWAM取得94.5%的平均成功率，其中标准环境约94.6%，域随机化环境约94.4%，所有指标超过LingBot-VA 2.0等方法，取得SOTA。 图9 RoboTwin 2.0评测结果 在RoboCasa365的50项任务评测中，LoopWAM取得49.5%的总体成功率，高于ABot-M0.6的46.6%。对于同时排除在专家训练数据和部署训练数据之外的16项未见组合任务，模型也取得了14.9%的成功率，展示了对未见任务组合的迁移能力。 图10 RoboCasa365评测结果 这两组实验均未进行额外的具身数据预训练，而是在预训练视频模型基础上，利用专家演示与部署轨迹进行学习。结合真实机器人实验，LoopWAM在真实与仿真的三个基准上均取得了最优成绩，为混合质量部署经验的利用价值提供了充分证据。 让每一次真实部署都带来可学习的经验，在真实部署中持续自提升，这是LoopWAM希望持续推进的方向。 signals.summary: Brett Adcock 於 10月22日公開本週全員大會錄像，披露 Figure 04 設計定型且零部件開始發貨、今夏第 1000 台 Figure 03 下線（相較 Figure 02 成本降九成以上）、自建眾包應用 Index 累計 3750 萬條視頻/126 萬次下載/112 國覆蓋、當週數據開支約 810 萬美元、與 Nscale 合作首期 35 億美元計劃擴至 60 億美元、現金餘額超 20 億美元，並預告 Helix 3.0 但未給細節；參照 Helix 2.5 於 9 月在 30 個住宅三類家務 420 次嘗試成功 237 次（約 56%）。

signals.evidence_quote: At 2.4 billion parameters—less than half the size of direct competitors like Qwen-RobotManip (4.7B)—the model achieves competitive performance
signals.summary: Alabia Insights 10月24日分析指出，2.4B 參數的 REKI 將跨幀記憶放在 action expert 模組（32 個 register token，3 幀窗口/1 秒間隔，21.8ms 動作塊僅增 0.1ms），姿態震盪從 18.6% 降至 4.1%；僅用 10 億幀公開數據（DROID/BridgeData V2/AgiBot World）預訓練，LIBERO-Plus 90.4% 高於 Qwen-RobotManip 89.0% 與 π0 85.7%，權重以 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 開放；但在 RoboCasa365 上 38.4% 明顯落後 Xiaomi-Robotics-1 57.4%。具體發布日期未知（來源為二手分析）。

REKI: How Compact VLA Models Are Redefining Robot Manipulation
Notícias sobre Robôs, IA e o Futuro do Trabalho
Industrial Automation Economy & Business Robots Industrial Robotics Analysis 🌐 🇧🇷 PT 🇺🇸 EN 🇪🇸 ES 🇨🇳 ZH REKI represents a critical inflection point in democratizing vision-language-action models for robotics . At 2.4 billion parameters—less than half the size of direct competitors like Qwen-RobotManip (4.7B)—the model achieves competitive performance through a fundamental architectural innovation: a memory mechanism based on learned registers operating within the action expert module rather than the vision-language layer. This architectural separation is technically elegant: 32 register tokens perform self-attention over prior frames (3-frame window, 1-second intervals) with negligible computational cost—merely 0.1 ms additional latency in a total 21.8 ms action chunk. The innovation solves a critical practical problem: pose oscillations affecting 18.6% of episodes in benchmarks reduce to 4.1%, indicating the model now captures sufficient temporal context to avoid perceptual aliasing. Economically, REKI catalyzes market reconfiguration in robotics. The model was pretrained exclusively on public data (1.0 billion frames from multiple sources: DROID, BridgeData V2, AgiBot World), eliminating dependence on proprietary datasets that historically created entry barriers. This substantially reduces development costs for startups and academic laboratories. Performance on LIBERO-Plus (90.4%) exceeds Qwen-RobotManip (89.0%) and π0 (85.7%), suggesting parameter efficiency, not raw scale, has become the dominant competitive factor. For robot manufacturers, this means 40-50% reduction in computational requirements without performance degradation—direct impact on embedded hardware costs and economic viability of distributed fleets. In labor markets, REKI accelerates transition of robot manipulation from highly structured to semi-structured environments. Tasks in picking, assembly, and food preparation—sectors employing 2.3 million workers in the US alone—face accelerated automation pressure. However, the model requires task-specific fine-tuning (3,000 steps with 50 demonstrations per task on UR5), creating demand for robot task engineering specialists and embodied AI annotation curators. Emerging professions in “robot prompt engineering” and “manipulation data curation” will partially offset manual manipulation displacement. Competitively, REKI differentiates through three vectors: (1) weight openness under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 versus closed competitors; (2) compiled latency of 21.8 ms on H100, viable for real-time control; (3) superior out-of-distribution generalization, with 13.8-point gains on Clean2Rand and 30.3 points under occlusion. Xiaomi-Robotics-1 remains superior on RoboCasa365 (57.4% vs 38.4%), indicating proprietary-data models still dominate highly variable environments. The trade-off persists: openness versus performance on extreme distributions. Over the next 18 months, we expect REKI to establish itself as the academic baseline, with adoption across 50+ university laboratories. Collaborative robotics companies (Universal Robots, ABB) will likely integrate fine-tuned variants by 2027. The critical milestone is demonstrating generalization across 5+ real tasks with fewer than 100 demonstrations per task—currently unachieved by any model. Quantization to INT8 and optimization for edge TPUs (not yet announced) will be necessary for penetration into cost-reduced robots (<$50k). Tasks in picking, assembly, and food preparation—sectors employing 2.3 million workers in the US alone—face accelerated automation pressure. However, the model requires task-specific fine-tuning (3,000 steps with 50 demonstrations per task on UR5), creating demand for robot task engineering specialists and embodied AI annotation curators. Emerging professions in “robot prompt engineering” and “manipulation data curation” will partially offset manual manipulation displacement. Competitively, REKI differentiates through three vectors: (1) weight openness under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 versus closed competitors; (2) compiled latency of 21.8 ms on H100, viable for real-time control; (3) superior out-of-distribution generalization, with 13.8-point gains on Clean2Rand and 30.3 points under occlusion. Xiaomi-Robotics-1 remains superior on RoboCasa365 (57.4% vs 38.4%), indicating proprietary-data models still dominate highly variable environments. The trade-off persists: openness versus performance on extreme distributions. Over the next 18 months, we expect REKI to establish itself as the academic baseline, with adoption across 50+ university laboratories. Collaborative robotics companies (Universal Robots, ABB) will likely integrate fine-tuned variants by 2027. The critical milestone is demonstrating generalization across 5+ real tasks with fewer than 100 demonstrations per task—currently unachieved by any model. Quantization to INT8 and optimization for edge TPUs (not yet announced) will be necessary for penetration into cost-reduced robots (<$50k). 宁德时代领投，松延动力被曝秘密递表港交所-36氪
推出9998元人形机器人的松延动力，传出了赴港上市的消息。
10月22日援引知情人士称，松延动力已以保密形式向港交所提交上市申请，可能筹集数亿美元，最快于2027年上市。目前相关讨论仍在进行，募资规模和时间安排可能调整。公司未回应彭博社的置评请求，也尚未公开确认这一计划。
松延动力成立于2023年9月。到今年3月，公司已累计完成九轮融资，最新一轮B轮融资规模累计近10亿元，由宁德时代系产业投资平台晨道资本领投，国科投资、京国盛基金、九合创投等机构跟投。在此之前的2月，公司已完成股份制改革。
资金之外，松延动力也在尝试打开家庭用户市场。
2025年10月22日，松延动力发布“Bumi小布米”，将这款人形机器人的起售价定在9998元。一年后，公司的上市消息传出，其产品也经历了从发布、登上春晚到面向用户交付的过程。
今年央视春晚，松延动力的机器人参与了蔡明、王天放出演的小品《奶奶的最爱》。3月的中国家电及消费电子博览会（AWE）上，创始人、董事长姜哲源将“小布米”交付给购买者。现场有家长购买这款产品，希望和孩子一起体验机器人。
“小布米”的定位也与这类需求相符：面向家庭，提供陪伴和图形化编程教育；面向机构，提供教育类解决方案。松延动力的其他产品还包括N系列、E系列双足人形机器人，以及仿生人头“小诺”等，覆盖导览、迎宾和展览展示等用途。
产品线铺得较多，与需求尚未集中有关。按照姜哲源此前介绍的情况，人形机器人可以进入的场景不少，但单个场景的需求量仍然有限，松延动力需要通过不同产品覆盖这些分散的市场。
今年3月，公司将“小布米”的全年交付目标定为万台。
松延动力推进交付的这一年，也是国内机器人企业集中寻求上市的一年。
5月18日，云深处科创板IPO申请获受理；次日，乐聚智能创业板IPO申请获受理。8月19日，宇树科技登陆科创板。此前相继完成融资和股改的机器人企业，开始陆续进入上市审核和公开交易环节。
进入9月，审核趋严的消息出现。路透社当月援引知情人士称，监管通过非正式“窗口指导”放缓部分人形机器人企业的上市进程。报道中的另一名知情人士同时强调，并不存在正式禁令。证监会未回应该报道的置评请求。
公开的投行反馈，也把讨论引向了收入和交付。财联社的采访显示，部分投行人员收到所在公司的提醒，行业地位不够突出的硬科技企业，上市进程可能受到影响。一家头部券商则将其解释为加强保荐机构的前端把关。
这些讨论集中在几个具体问题上：订单来自哪里，客户是否会持续采购，交付增加之后亏损能否收窄。依靠政府支持项目、关联交易或一次性收益获得的收入，能否延续到下一年，也需要进一步验证。
已经上市的宇树科技，则经历了股价的大幅起落。
上市首日，宇树收盘报845元，较发行价上涨约460%，盘中一度达到1100元。此后股价回调，到10月15日触及404.03元的盘中低点。10月22日收盘价回升至520元，较这一低点反弹约29%，但仍比上市首日高点低约53%。
宇树近期披露的股票交易异常波动公告，也提到了市场预期与商业化进度之间的风险：人形机器人仍处于商业化早期，一旦大规模应用落地慢于预期，收入增长和业绩兑现就可能受到影响。
未上市企业仍在获得资金，只是大额融资的数量已经减少。
盖世具身智能的不完全统计显示，今年9月，国内具身机器人及核心零部件领域披露49笔融资，其中10亿元级融资只有两笔。今年4月和6月，同等规模的融资各有10笔。融资事件仍然密集，但单笔大额融资已不如此前高峰期频繁。
智元的上市时间表也在变化。这家公司今年7月启动港股上市筹备，到了10月，又传出开展新一轮融资的消息。《财经》10月13日援引投资人称，这轮融资规模约10亿至15亿元，已接近收尾，估值约500亿元，新融资可能影响其年内完成IPO的安排。智元尚未回应上述融资、估值和上市进展。
松延动力此次被曝选择的香港市场，已有相应的保密申请机制。2025年5月推出的“科企专线”，允许符合条件的特专科技公司和生物科技公司以保密形式递交上市申请，减少经营策略、专有技术和上市计划被过早披露的风险。松延动力拟采用哪一套具体上市规则，目前尚不清楚。
目前，松延动力的上市估值和募资用途仍未披露。“小布米”的年度万台交付目标完成多少，9998元起的产品能带来多少收入和毛利，尚需等待公司公布更完整的经营数据。

四川具身科技融1亿，把表情做在投影上
四川具身人形机器人科技完成超 1 亿元 Pre-A 轮融资。这轮融资与人形机器人中试熟化项目支持相协同，形成省、市、县三级国资联动的格局。资金将主要用于其标志性产品人形机器人"爱湫"的迭代研发、万台级生产基地建设以及销售体系的搭建，新一轮融资也已同步启动。三级国资联动支持，说明地方对这个赛道有产业层面的期待。中试熟化的说法，指的是从样机走向量产的那一段工程验证。 公司的产品定位叫 Emotion Native，把情感陪伴作为产品的原生目标，让本体形态、语言理解、面部表达与动作控制共同服务于人与机器人的长期相处。这个提法和常见的"AI Native"不同，它假设家庭场景里的价值不只在完成任务，还在于每天相处时的那种自然感。把情感写进产品定义，是一个需要勇气的选择，因为它很难被量化。但它也逼着团队把模糊的感受翻译成具体的设计参数。 最直观的体现是面部。爱湫采用 3D 超短焦投影方案，把仿生表情投射在立体面部上，官方称这是国内独创的做法。相比用屏幕或机械结构做脸，投影的成本更低、量产更容易，还能通过数字内容适配一键切换形象与表情，灵活呈现文旅角色或品牌 IP。同一套硬件因此获得了持续更新表达方式的空间。投影方案的另一面是，它在强光下的对比度和色彩表现都受物理限制。 价格给出了一个坐标。爱湫 9.8 万元起售，在中小型双足人形机器人里属于偏低的位置。这个定价把"陪伴体验"和"购置成本"一起放进了用户的选择题，而不只是比谁的动作更灵活。对一个还没有形成标准答案的品类来说，先给出一个可比较的价格锚，本身就是一种策略。九万八这个价格，把双足人形从展台拉到了可以认真考虑的范围。 难点在于长期使用。真实用户会转换话题、改变需求，也会用语气和动作传递没说出口的意思，机器人需要持续理解情境，让语言、表情和行动保持一致。演示视频里做到这些不难，难的是连续几个月每天都做到。所谓陪伴的壁垒，其实藏在每一次平淡的日常交互里。演示里的一致性和日常里的一致性，是两件完全不同的事。后者需要长期的数据积累和场景打磨，没有捷径。 投影面部是一个聪明的差异化，也是一次成本妥协 。 它在亲和力上占了便宜，但在强光环境下的可读性、长期投影的亮度衰减、以及"看起来像投影"的心理感受上，都有天然的短板。这条路能不能走通，取决于用户到底是在买一个机器人，还是在买一个愿意被当成家人的存在。差异化能否转化为复购，取决于用户第二次、第三次还愿不愿意打开它。 返回搜狐，查看更多 阅读 ( ) 平台声明 该文观点仅代表作者本人，搜狐号系信息发布平台，搜狐仅提供信息存储空间服务。

📡 VLA 社交情报 | 2026-10-26

🔴 高价值信号（一级）
- [开源项目] NVIDIA / Pollen Robotics：开源消费级双足机器人 Microduck 在 2026-10 GTC 柏林黄仁勋主题演讲中亮相后走红，据报道次日（2026-10-23）预订量超过 2 万台，预计圣诞节前交付。它采用仿真环境训练策略、再迁移到真机的技术路线，并开放社区训练和分享动作库。对 VLA 的意义：NVIDIA 通过「仿真工具链 + 开源硬件 + 社区动作库」闭环，把仿真到真机（sim2real）数据采集成本外部化，同时降低开发者参与门槛；不过 2 万台是预订量并非交付量，官方未公布价格、自由度与算力配置，第三方稳定性测评也缺失。
  https://aiwiki.clawcaff.com/nvidia-microduck/

📊 动态摘要（二级）
- 松延动力（Noetix）：据报道该公司已以保密方式向港交所递交上市申请，计划 2027 年挂牌；累计完成 9 轮融资，B 轮近 10 亿元由宁德时代晨道资本领投，估值超 20 亿；消费级人形产品「小布米」定价 9998 元、身高 94cm、21 自由度，主打家庭陪伴与少儿编程。含义：万元级人形本体压低门槛，但其能力集中在稳定行走、语音跟随等陪伴场景，未涉及 VLA 操作策略，与触觉 + VLA 主线交叉有限。
  https://www.163.com/dy/article/LA0JJHN70556HT7C.html?referFrom=

🔭 趋势观察：今日两条信号都来自消费级、低成本机器人本体，并非来自 VLA 操作能力方面的进展：NVIDIA 通过与开源硬件绑定的仿真训练生态扩展开发者规模，松延动力则依靠供应链自研把整机价格压到万元以内。两者共同反映的趋势是，具身智能的商业叙事正下沉到可及性，但都没有给出操作策略层面的技术证据。

【机器人】松延动力传港股IPO：9998元小布米，宁德时代晨道资本押注
Source publication date: 2026-10-24
【机器人】松延动力传港股IPO：9998元小布米，宁德时代晨道资本押注,布米,动作,编程,ipo,松延动力,知名企业,人形机器人,宁德时代晨道
【机器人】松延动力传港股IPO：9998元小布米，宁德时代晨道资本押注
用微信扫码二维码
分享至好友和朋友圈
一、春晚出圈的万元人形，把门槛打下来了
在多数人形机器人还停留在几十万、上百万的高价样机阶段的时候，松延动力直接抛出了定价 9998元的消费陪伴人形机器人小布米 ，一下子把人形机器人拉到普通家庭能够触碰的区间。这款身高94厘米、21个自由度的机器人，不是实验室里只能做固定演示的展品，主打家庭陪伴、少儿编程教学，也是登上央视春晚舞台出圈的那款产品。春晚的舞台考验很苛刻，团队在短时间内反复调试步态、动作交互，让小布米完成舞蹈、互动表演，也向市场证明，消费级人形机器人可以稳定落地，而不是只存在于宣传片里。
它的定位很克制，不追求极致的全能能力，优先做好孩子的编程玩伴、家庭语音互动助手，搭配图形化拖拽编程，小朋友也能自己给机器人编排动作。线下已经走进不少中小学科创课堂，也和孩子王等渠道合作，在门店设置体验点位，普通家长可以带着孩子上手体验。这种贴近普通人的落地方式，和很多只面向B端客户的人形机器人企业形成明显差异。
二、自研控本+快速迭代，支撑起产品的底层底气
能做到万元以内定价，核心不是简单缩减功能，而是松延动力在核心零部件、结构材料、运动算法上做了自研整合。 自研域控制器+轻量化复合材料结构，在控制整机重量的同时，稳住运动控制的稳定性 ，再加上国产化供应链整合，才把成本压到消费市场可以接受的水平。同时小布米支持持续OTA升级，和智能手机、新能源车一样，后续可以不断更新动作库、交互模型、教育内容，硬件交付只是服务的起点。
从创立到现在，这家公司的迭代节奏一直很快，43天就能完成初代机器人从概念到整机落地。春晚项目里，团队一个月内完成二十多次动作版本调整，快速适配舞台场景需求。背后的团队以清华、浙大背景的年轻研发人员为主，聚焦运动控制、多模态交互这两个核心方向，避开了全栈大而全的路线，集中资源攻克陪伴场景需要的稳定行走、语音跟随、安全交互能力。
三、9轮融资冲刺港股IPO，它的商业模式怎么跑
消息显示松延动力已经以保密方式向港交所递交申请，计划2027年挂牌上市。资本层面的热度很直观： 累计完成9轮融资，B轮近10亿元由宁德时代晨道资本领投，公司估值已经超过20亿 。产业资本愿意大手笔投入，看重的不只是春晚带来的流量，而是它已经跑通的商业模式雏形：硬件售卖为基础，叠加教育内容、编程生态、OTA增值服务。
简单来说，它不是靠一台机器人赚一次性差价。硬件卖给家庭、学校之后，后续可以持续更新编程课程、互动内容，和编程猫等内容方合作扩充素材库；同时大量家庭真实使用的数据，又能反向优化运动算法、交互模型，形成数据闭环。订单层面，首发阶段首批机器很快售罄，校园、亲子门店的渠道持续铺开，慢慢从单点演示走向规模化交付。当然挑战同样明显：消费机器人售后、用户留存、复购生态，都是接下来IPO路上要持续验证的考题。

分享到： 微信扫码分享 链接已复制，去 Ins 分享吧！ Microduck 是一款由 Pollen Robotics 生产、现归属英伟达的 开源消费级机器人 。2026 年 10 月，英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋在 GTC 柏林大会主题演讲中与一群 Microduck 互动的视频在网上走红，第二天预订量就超过 2 万台。 这个数字由 Hugging Face 首席执行官 Clem Delangue 在社交平台公布。Microduck 预计能在圣诞节前交付，多家媒体判断它可能成为今年最畅销的机器人产品，而且这个称号未必只属于孩子——宣传视频里玩这些机器人的更多是成年人。 它的走红路径很有代表性：一款开源小机器人在 GPU 巨头的主题演讲上出现几十秒，成本极低，效果却胜过多数消费电子的投放。但真正值得记录的不是营销，而是它背后的三层股权与训练链路，那才是这类产品能快速迭代的原因。 Microduck 是 Pollen Robotics 的开源设备。Pollen Robotics 于 2025 年被 Hugging Face 收购，而 Hugging Face 又在 2026 年 9 月被英伟达收购，所以它现在属于英伟达。这是 Hugging Face 体系下的第二款机器人，上一款是 Reachy Mini。 项目 信息 产品名 Microduck 形态 鸭子造型的小型双足机器人 生产方 Pollen Robotics（开源硬件） 当前归属 英伟达（2026 年 9 月收购 Hugging Face 后纳入） 前代产品 Reachy Mini 训练方式 仿真环境训练后迁移真机，基础动作随设备出厂 交互能力 踩小碎步走路、坐下、原地倒下假装睡觉、按语音指令空翻 预订量 2026 年 10 月 23 日次日超过 2 万台 交付时间 预计圣诞节前 价格 官方未公布 这些机器人使用英伟达的技术栈训练：先在仿真环境中教会走路、坐下、站立等基础动作，再把策略随设备出厂。用户可以为自己的机器人训练新技巧，再分享给社区。这条「仿真训练 + 真机迁移」的路径，与业内用生成模型造训练数据属于同一思路——都是把真实世界的采集成本转移到可无限复现的虚拟环境里。 开放程度带来一个直接后果：设备的性能上限取决于背后的仿真环境和硬件栈，而不是单台机器人的设计精度。用户可以自己训练新动作并回传社区，社区积累的动作库会反过来成为产品的护城河。英伟达同时握有仿真训练栈与硬件，两层收购让它能把这条链路完整收进自己的平台，这正是它与其他玩具机器人厂商的根本差别。 过去两年人形与四足机器人的新闻集中在工业场景，负载、续航、精度是核心指标，价格动辄数万到数十万美元。Microduck 走的是完全相反的一端：低成本、低负载、以娱乐与教育为主。这类产品对具身智能的价值不在营收，而在数据与开发者生态——它把「给机器人写动作」这件事的门槛降到了普通爱好者能参与的水平，等于免费扩张了仿真环境的真实用户反馈。 可比的对象是 Agility Digit 5 这类工业人形，以及 宇树 在四足与小型人形上的消费线。三者都在做「仿真到真机」的迁移，只是把成本结构做在不同位置：工业机追求可靠性，消费机追求可及性，开源机追求可修改性。 一款开源小机器人在 GPU 巨头的主题演讲上走红的成本很低，但它给出了消费级机器人与仿真训练结合的一个现成样本。更深一层看，英伟达通过连续收购把「仿真工具链—开源硬件—社区动作库」串成闭环，这条闭环的收益不在卖机器人，而在让更多人用它的仿真与训练栈。 需要泼的冷水同样明显。2 万台是预订量不是交付量，圣诞节前能否兑现产能仍是未知数；官方未公布价格、续航、自由度、负载与算力配置，也未见第三方对动作稳定性与耐用性的测评。作为礼品与教育产品，这些缺失还可以接受；作为具身智能的研究平台，参数透明度不足会限制它被严肃使用的可能。对关注本体的读者，它更适合当作「开源硬件 + 仿真训练」的模式样本，而不是性能基准。

CASBOT raises several hundred million yuan in A++ financing for robot production — Korthos
Source publication date: 2026-10-26
CASBOT raises several hundred million yuan in A++ financing for robot production
China's Zhongke Huiling is directing new capital toward scaled deliveries and embodied control systems, following a previous A round led by Lens Technology.
Structured intelligence on robotics, autonomy, infrastructure, markets, and the broader machine economy.
Image: CASBOT Beijing-based Zhongke Huiling, developer of the CASBOT robotics range, has completed an A++ financing of several hundred million yuan. Investors include Zhilai Investment, Yonghua Investment, Maotian Investment, Yuanhe Chenkun, Guoke Kezhi and Luning Investment, according to the 26 October financing announcement. The capital will support product manufacturing and deliveries, development of embodied control models and market expansion. Founded in 2023, the company develops robot hardware, dexterous hands and control systems. Its announced portfolio includes the full-size CASBOT 02 humanoid, the wheeled-arm CASBOT W2 and the smaller CASBOT Mini. The business previously raised nearly RMB100 million in a June 2025 A round led by precision-manufacturing group Lens Technology. Footwear production is one of its principal industrial applications. CASBOT began testing an insole-stamping robot at a factory in Putian in August 2025 and subsequently secured work with footwear manufacturers. In its latest operating update, the company reports more than RMB400 million of footwear-robot orders on hand in 2026 and equipment production schedules reaching several thousand units. Its CASBOT PA perception-to-action model links visual observations, action generation, kinematics and execution on physical hardware. The company says the lightweight model supports training on a single consumer GPU and has been tested with robot arms at footwear-production workstations. Those deployments provide task data for improving manipulation policies and adapting systems to specific factory processes. CASBOT is also developing systems for hazardous underground work. A joint venture established in June 2025 with Shandong Zhaojin and Shandong Zhongkuang focuses on mining applications including explosives loading and safety patrols. The company says a loading robot has entered field training in a working mine, with development addressing remote operation, dust, moisture and unstable communications.

signals.evidence_quote: On 21 October, Agile Robots and NVIDIA launched the research humanoid Agile ONE SN at NVIDIA GTC Berlin.
signals.summary: 2026-10-21，Agile Robots 与 NVIDIA 在 NVIDIA GTC Berlin 发布研究型人形平台 Agile ONE SN：基于 NVIDIA Isaac GR00T 构建，1.4m/43kg、71 自由度、双臂各一只 WUJI 触觉五指手，运行于 Jetson Thor，随机预装 GR00T 1.7 开源 VLA 模型，计划 2027 年初发售。

signals.evidence_quote: その2日前、ベルリンで開催された「Invest in Germany Summit」において、NVIDIAはAgile Robotsへの投資計画を発表しました。
signals.summary: 据同一通稿，NVIDIA 在柏林 Invest in Germany Summit 宣布了投资 Agile Robots 的计划；原文仅称该峰会发生在 GTC Berlin 发布（10月21日）「两天前」，未给出精确日期，金额与条款均未说明。

signals.evidence_quote: Agile Robots, AUDI AG, Dassault Systèmes và NVIDIA cũng công bố một dự án hợp tác tại nhà máy Ingolstadt của Audi.
signals.person_or_entity: Agile Robots / AUDI AG / Dassault Systèmes / NVIDIA
signals.summary: 同一通稿宣布与 Audi、Dassault Systèmes 在 Audi 因戈尔施塔特工厂的 Production Lab 联合验证：移动人形从料箱取件并按顺序排列供最终装配，该工位日均约百万次操作；工作单元先在 DELMIA + NVIDIA Omniverse 虚拟孪生中测试。通稿未给出该项目的具体启动日期。

Ứng dụng: robot hình người trong hoạt động logistics của Audi Agile Robots, AUDI AG, Dassault Systèmes và NVIDIA cũng công bố một dự án hợp tác tại nhà máy Ingolstadt của Audi. Tại Phòng thí nghiệm sản xuất Audi, các robot hình người có khả năng di chuyển sẽ lấy linh kiện từ các thùng chứa và sắp xếp chúng theo đúng trình tự để phục vụ công đoạn lắp ráp cuối cùng, một nhiệm vụ được thực hiện khoảng một triệu lần mỗi ngày. Cụm làm việc này trước tiên được thử nghiệm trong môi trường bản sao ảo DELMIA được tăng tốc nhờ các thư viện NVIDIA Omniverse. Diana 7 và Diana 3: một giao diện, từ phòng thí nghiệm đến tải trọng công nghiệp Diana 7 mở rộng khả năng của Franka Research 3 lên tải trọng lớn hơn và tầm với xa hơn, trong khi Diana 3 đưa cùng nền tảng điều khiển lực vào các nghiên cứu ở cấp độ nhập môn. Cả hai đều có độ lặp lại ±0,05 mm và độ chính xác điều khiển lực tương đối là 0,5 N, và cả hai đều hỗ trợ FCI, vì vậy mã của Franka Research 3 có thể chuyển trực tiếp sang Diana. Diana 3 vẫn giữ nguyên thiết kế bảy bậc tự do, cảm biến mô-men xoắn tại các khớp và điều khiển linh hoạt phục vụ các thao tác chính xác, tự động hóa phòng thí nghiệm và xử lý mẫu. Diana 7, được trưng bày tại Hội chợ Công nghiệp Quốc tế Trung Quốc lần thứ 26 ở Thượng Hải (từ ngày 12 đến ngày 16 tháng 10), có tải trọng 7 kg và tầm với 923 mm, nhẹ hơn 2 kg so với phiên bản trước. Giới thiệu về Agile Robots Được thành lập tại Munich vào năm 2018 bởi các nhà nghiên cứu robot học đến từ Trung tâm Hàng không Vũ trụ Đức (DLR), Agile Robots cung cấp các giải pháp robot ứng dụng AI và có hơn 3.500 nhân viên trên toàn thế giới. Cùng với các công ty thành viên BÄR Automation, Franka Robotics, idealworks và Krause Automation, công ty hoạt động trên tất cả các lĩnh vực robot ứng dụng AI. Liquid AI 发布开放权重基础模型系列 LFM3，六个约 2B 参数模型统一 tri-hybrid 骨干，视觉版本强调具身推理，并演示机械臂操作与 VLA 端侧推理，LIBERO 自报成功率 96.2%。了解 LFM3 架构与机器人应用详情。
技术 Liquid AI 于 10 月 27 日发布开放权重的 LFM3 基础模型系列，六个约 2B 参数模型统一采用 tri-hybrid 骨干，视觉版本强调具身推理，并演示了机械臂操作、视觉语言导航与 VLA 端侧推理能力。 摘要 Liquid AI 于 10 月 27 日发布开放权重的 LFM3 基础模型系列，六个约 2B 参数模型统一采用 tri-hybrid 骨干，视觉版本强调具身推理，并演示了机械臂操作、视觉语言导航与 VLA 端侧推理能力。 01 LFM3 系列首发 6 个约 2B 参数模型，覆盖文本、视觉、音频、omni 与决策，全部开放权重上架 Hugging Face。 02 新 tri-hybrid 骨干在 24 层中混用门控短卷积、滑窗注意力与全局注意力，出自覆盖 14 种硬件组合的架构搜索。 03 LFM3-VL-2B 首次支持视频输入，强调空间与具身推理，配套自研 164M 参数视觉编码器。 04 官方演示了机械臂仿真操作、视觉语言导航及跨 15 种机器人本体的 VLA 单一通用模型，自报 LIBERO 平均成功率 96.2%。 05 所有跨模型对标与端侧吞吐数字均为厂商自报，权重公开后有待独立跑分验证。 Liquid AI 发布新一代 LFM3 基础模型系列，包含文本、视觉、音频、全模态与决策五类共六个模型，全部从 LFM3-1.7B-Base 骨干特化，权重同步开放在 Hugging Face。新系列采用经硬件在环架构搜索得到的三重混合骨干，在 24 层中混用门控短卷积、滑窗注意力与全局注意力，兼顾端侧速度与长上下文。其中视觉模型 LFM3-VL-2B 首次支持视频输入并强调空间与具身推理，官方还展示了将其微调用于机械臂仿真操作、视觉语言导航及跨 15 种本体的 VLA 通用模型，在 LIBERO 套件自报平均成功率 96.2%，可在 Jetson AGX Orin 上 50 毫秒内生成动作块。各项对标成绩均为厂商自报口径，尚待独立验证。 技术 VLM/VLA/世界模型 技术 算力芯片 公司 Agility Robotics 技术 VLA模型 技术 VLM/VLA/世界模型 公司 蚂蚁灵波 技术 VLM/VLA/世界模型 公司 非夕科技 公司 智在无界 公司 仙工智能 技术 VLM/VLA/世界模型

Machenta Raises $40 Million to Teach Robots New Tasks From One Demonstration
London startup Machenta has raised $40 million to pursue robots that can pick up new tasks from a single demonstration , without a fresh round of training each time. Its approach uses simulation to teach a model how to learn, then a real-world demonstration to tell it what to do. Show all Business Insider reports a $40 million seed round co-led by Creandum and Union Square Ventures. This configuration is designed so the robot can complete the entire sequence of "move — manipulate — transport — hand over" in one go. On October 28, PHYMI officially launched its first robot product, Sagi, nicknamed "Saqima." None of these three scenarios involve complex tasks. What they share is the need for the robot to switch back and forth between moving, manipulating, transporting, and handing over. Cognition Layer — Understand where to pick up from and who to deliver to, organizing task steps; Behavior Layer — Determine how to move and what actions to take, bridging operational steps; Contact Layer — Rapidly adjust based on force-tactile feedback and proprioceptive state, avoiding unstable grasps or improper contact. This is PHYMI BRAIN 1.0, the asynchronous multi-frequency multimodal architecture powering Sagi — three layers each running at their own required frequencies, then coordinating through information connections, balancing long-horizon task planning with local action correction. Connecting humans and robots is PHYMI LINK: state objectives, check progress, change requirements mid-stream — and when information is insufficient or beyond capability, the robot can turn around and ask humans for help. In 2018 he joined autonomous driving company DeepRoute.ai, progressing from hardware through to Robotaxi operations, product, data, mass production, and after-sales service. In 2026, Liu added another identity — founder of PHYMI. Starting in 2024, he closely tracked embodied intelligence developments, poring over papers and continuously studying upstream supply chains and technical approaches. By late 2025, he judged the timing for entrepreneurship ripe: on one hand, robot supply chains had matured enough that startups no longer needed to expend enormous effort filling gaps in bodies and hardware; on the other, AI-driven technical and data paradigms were becoming clear enough to begin forming genuinely long-term valuable technical accumulation. Ziegler, Charlie Songhurst and many more. I spent years managing teams on Renault Group assembly lines. Robots handled the fixed, repetitive tasks; anything that changed still fell to people. Humanoid robots won't replace industrial robots, but they can take on everything those robots can't: tasks that need two arms, a torso, or moving around the line. The hardware is no longer the bottleneck. The software is: every new task takes months of engineering and hundreds of hours of training data. In most factories, tasks change too often for that to pay off. So we're taking a different path from end-to-end models trained on massive datasets that don’t exist yet. Built on years of research at Inria by my co-founders Jean-Baptiste Mouret and Serena Ivaldi, our model doesn't just copy a movement: it understands what the task is for, adapts when parts, positions or context change, and works on any platform, from industrial arms to humanoids. Bleu Robotics raises €5M to scale humanoid robot deployment
By Lydia Arundel Share Les cofondateurs de Bleu Robotics, Benoit Berkoukchi, CEO, Jean‑Baptiste Mouret, CTO et Serena Ivaldi, directrice du board scientifique, prennent la pose dans leurs locaux. Paris, France. 9 octobre 2026. SHARE Bleu Robotics , a startup developing AI models for industrial humanoid robots, has raised a €5 million pre-seed round, co-led by Contrarian Ventures and OVNI Capital, with participation from Kvanted, WEPA Ventures, Motier Ventures and Charlie Songhurst, technology investor and board member at Meta The company plans to utilise the funds to grow its team and scale its software solution across industries, pursuing its goal of reducing the full humanoid robot deployment process to one hour or less. Five million industrial robots were operating globally in 2025, according to the International Federation of Robotics . These robots are designed to repeat fixed tasks and cannot adapt to the high-mix, low-volume production now common in modern manufacturing, so human workers still do much of the work. Humanoid robots help to automate a wider range of complex tasks. While hardware has advanced in recent years, software development has struggled to keep pace, limiting real-world deployment. Interact Analysis found that out of the 20,000+ humanoids produced last year, only 10% reached real-world applications. Currently, most robots rely on end-to-end models that learn everything in a single black box and require massive amounts of data to achieve production-ready reliability. As a result, deployment is costly and time-consuming for manufacturers, often requiring hundreds of hours of training data, with no guarantee the robot will perform reliably. Bleu’s technology removes the need for those large task-specific datasets and long training cycles, enabling manufacturers to deploy robots cost-effectively and at scale. Bleu Robotic’s abductive learning model lets the robot learn a new task from as few as ten operator demonstrations, while maintaining the explainability required for industrial safety and the 99%+ accuracy production lines demand. The model eliminates the need for large amounts of training data by inferring the most likely intent behind an operator’s demonstration, including the task’s goal and constraints, and determining how to reproduce it reliably. The software can be plugged into any humanoid platform. Operators can teach it new tasks at the workstation using Bleu’s training devices and handheld grippers that eliminate the need for coding, and can retrain the same robot as production needs change or move it to another site. Benoît Berkoukchi, co-founder of Bleu Robotics, said, “Humanoid robots in manufacturing are the next automotive sector, with the potential to help Europe and the US reshore production. But most robotics companies are trying to train humanoids with millions of data points and build fully general-purpose models. That approach isn’t suited to manufacturing. There isn’t enough data on factory work, and there won’t be internet-scale data, the kind LLMs were built on, for robots for a long time. Our methodology means we can do more with less.” Thomas Poitrineau, investor at Contrarian Ventures, said, “We were attracted to Bleu Robotics because of their ambitious choice to rethink how humanoid robotics software should work from first principles. It’s rare to find a company led by two world-class robotics researchers and a manufacturing expert, which is also why their software works differently from their competition. Their goal is far bigger than simply making the best model in a lab. It’s an approach that can already scale, putting robots to work in factories within months rather than years.” Add Engineer Live to your Google News feed TAGGED: AI models automation Bleu Robotics humanoid robotics Share This Article Facebook Copy Link Print Leave a Comment Your email address will not be published.
